newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Chubais says 1997 budget cannot be met.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Chubais says 1997 budget cannot be met.

text.p: Russia cannot fulfil its 1997 budget and will have to cut spending, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Wednesday.

"We have to recognise that it is not possible to fulfil this budget," Chubais, responsible for finances and economic reforms, told the upper house of parliament. "This year's planned revenues are 100 trillion roubles more than is possible for the state."

Chubais said the Russian government had drawn up a plan for sequestering spending -- cutting the amount of money spent across the board. He is due to present the plans to the State Duma lower house of parliament on April 23.
Chubais said Russia had brought in just 56.6 percent of planned revenues in the first quarter, while expenditure was 62.8 percent of planned levels.

Tax revenues were a dismal 39 percent of planned revenues in the first quarter, but some of the shortfall had been made up from customs revenues, which were 15 percent more than outlined in the budget.

"The monstrous budget crisis is at the root of all the troubles and it throws into question whether the state can perform its functions," Chubais said. "It is not possible to finance all scheduled payments under these circumstances."
